en: The Ritual Manual for the Sequence of Recitation of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra, Part 2:
Chapter on the Maintenance of Purifying Conduct. Chapter Two on the Maintenance of Purifying Conduct, also titled "The Chapter on Increasing and Protecting Pure Conduct.
Abiding with single-minded devotion and profound reverence, one prostrates by casting the five limbs upon the ground.
I take refuge in the Perfectly Awakened Ones of the ten directions, Who possess the three bodies throughout the three times;
I take refuge in all Mahāyāna teachings, And in the assembly of those who do not regress from bodhi;
I take refuge in the true words of the vidyās, And in all secret mudrās.
With the pure karma of body, speech, and mind, I reverently and immeasurably pay homage.
The mantra of the skillful means for taking refuge is:
*Oṃ namas-sarva-buddhānāṃ gagana-garbhe*. Placing the right knee on the ground and joining the palms, one should contemplate and confess previously committed sinful karma.
"Accumulated by me through ignorance, I have committed various transgressions of body,
speech, and mind; because my heart was shrouded by greed, hatred, and delusion, [I have erred] toward the Buddha,
the True Dharma, the Noble Sangha, my parents and two teachers, spiritual friends, and immeasurable sentient beings."
Throughout the beginningless flow of birth and death, I have committed extremely grave and inexhaustible sins;
now, in the presence of the Buddhas of the ten directions currently living, I confess them all and vow never to commit them again.
The mantra for the expedient means of emerging from transgression is as follows:

“Namo to the Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, To the treasury of the True Dharma of the three kinds of eternal bodies, And to the assembly of the Great Mind of Bodhi with its supreme vows; I now take refuge in all of them with perfect sincerity.”
The mantra for the skillful means of taking refuge is as follows:
"I purify this body, free from all defilements, along with the bodies, speech, and minds of the three times,
in numbers exceeding the dust motes of oceans of buddha-fields, and offer them to all the Tathāgatas."
The mantra for the skillful means of offering the body is as follows:

"The jewel of the supreme vow of the pure bodhicitta, I now arouse it to deliver all living beings Who are entangled by the accumulation of birth and suffering, And whose bodies are harmed by ignorance."
Rescuing, gathering, and providing refuge to bring about liberation, you shall always benefit all sentient beings.
Throughout the infinite worlds of the ten directions, the ocean-like assemblies of the Perfectly Enlightened Ones,
by means of their various skillful powers of expedient means, as well as the sons of the Buddhas for the sake of all living beings—
"Whatever meritorious deeds have been cultivated, I now rejoice in them all.
The mantra for the skillful means of rejoicing is:
"I now entreat all the Tathāgatas, the Greatly Awakened Ones who save the world with their Bodhicitta."
"I only pray that throughout the realms of the ten directions, you will constantly let fall the rain of Dharma from great clouds.
The mantra for the exhortation of skillful means says:
"May those dwelling as ordinary beings quickly cast off this body, which is a collection of manifold sufferings."
When I attain the Stainless Ground (*vimalā-bhūmi*), I shall abide securely in the essence of the pure Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).
Whatever various virtuous deeds I have cultivated To benefit all sentient beings,
I now dedicate them all correctly, To eliminate the suffering of birth and death and reach Bodhi.
The mantra for the skillful means of dedication is:
Oṃ saptāttahato ghatta niḥrīyatana prajñe game gasamumna raṣpara na saṃmāye hūṃ. The Seal of Entering the Buddha-Samaya:
To purify the defilements of the three karmas, one binds the Samaya-seal.
First, join the hands of concentration and wisdom, erecting both *śūnyatā*-mudrās;
touch all the limbs while reciting the words of truth.
The mantra for entering the Buddha-samaya is as follows:
*Svā mu khe piṇḍe oṃ amatsamme tsamme tsamma ye svāhā.* The Seal of the Arising of the Dharmadhātu: With the hands of Prajñāsamādhi, form both vajra-fists;
place the two thumbs within the palms, and keep the index fingers (the "wind" and "banner") perfectly straight.
Place the mudrā upon the forehead, then circle it around the body and scatter it downward;
contemplate that the body and all phenomena are equal to the dharmadhātu, stainless like space.
The mantra for the arising of the dharmadhātu is as follows:
The Vajrasattva mudrā: bind the Vajrajñāna seal;
with the hands of śamatha and vipaśyanā turned back-to-back, form the wheels of earth, water, fire, and wind.
The left and right hands hold each other; the two empty palms rotate separately and then join within the wisdom-palms. This is called the Dharma-Wheel, the most supreme and auspicious mudrā.
The mantra of Vajrasattva is as follows:
Having recited this mantra, one should abide in meditative equipoise and clearly contemplate that this body of mine is indeed the Holder of the Vajra.
The Armor Vajra Mudrā: First perform the *tripuṭa*;
with the two wind-wheels (the index fingers) held together above the fire-wheel (the middle fingers), join them at the upper joints of the middle fingers;
the two space-fingers (the thumbs) are placed side by side.
And within the palms of the hands, visualize the syllable *raṃ* as a wheel of fire.
Like a bright pearl, place the syllable *raṃ* upon the crown of the head.
The Armor Mantra (*kavaca-mantra*) is as follows:
Next, one should contemplate Akṣobhya, who is able to subdue all great obstacles.
The syllable RAṂ emits blazing light and flames, encircling and adorning his entire body.
The mantra of Akṣobhya is as follows:
First, bind the samaya seal; next, the immovable sword mudrā, then offer argha water.
Again, present the vajrāsana, followed by incense, flowers, and so forth—to the stainless, immovable Lord.
Visualize the syllables appearing before you, one cubit’s distance away,
blazing like the radiance of the morning sun.
By reciting the true meaning, one is able to eliminate all obstacles.
Furthermore, the site of the path of purification is cleansed, with all faults and afflictions entirely removed;
its appearance is like empty space.
Looking downward, one observes the wind-circle (vāyu-maṇḍala), where black light and flames spread forth.
Next is the water wheel with the syllable *vaṃ*, its color like that of the milk ocean.
Next, one contemplates the syllable *a* of the earth, golden-yellow in color in all four directions.
Regarding these four gates of contemplation for the syllables above, one should first recite the homage in each case.
From this vajra-circle, the universal manifestations of all dharmas appear;
behold clearly the Lord Muni, seated upon a lotus flower of a hundred jewels.
A multitude of wondrous flowers gush forth in a circle, with billions upon billions of lotuses in attendance.
Upon each lotus flower, there is a World-Honored One of immeasurable majesty and virtue.
Within the vast celestial palaces, jeweled pillars stand in rows;
there are banners, streamers, and flower garlands, as well as auspicious vases and *ākā* water.
Clouds of fragrant flowers rain down everywhere, while clusters of precious jewels circulate throughout;
nets of light hang as delicate canopies, mutually reflecting all wondrous forms.
The palace towers high and wide like a great tree, its brilliance penetrating and pervading the entire Dharma-realm.
Inverted canopies spread with jade-like blossoms, Flowers and leaves everywhere fragrant.
A thousand varieties of exquisite fruits Are scattered profusely across the Dharma feast.
Skillfully colored mani-lamps Dangle beside, as celestial robes descend.
Fragrant medicines contain exquisite flavors, and fragrant delicacies are prepared with rare tastes;
celestial music plays wondrous tones, their harmonious melodies sounding pleasing to the mind.
The Cloud Terrace is without limit, wonderfully presenting all manner of offerings.
With both self-power and the empowerment of the Buddhas, And with a mind that pervades the entire Dharma-realm,
Simply by reciting this mantra, One performs a vast and magnificent offering.
The Mantra of the Vidyārājñī Ākāśagarbha is as follows:
All phenomena are unborn, for their self-nature is fundamentally quiescent;
contemplating this mantra, place the letter A within it.
It transforms into the Honored One Vairocana, universally manifesting as a multitude of beings as numerous as dust motes.
Rays of light pervade the entire Dharma-realm, awakening beings according to their dispositions.
Upon a great lotus king, one should clearly visualize the Honored Muni;
within the white tuft of hair between the Honored One’s brows, there further appears the Lord of Radiance.
Having clearly visualized the Sovereign Lord, one should then perform the rite of empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*).
The heart-mantra of Mahāvairocana is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām ā*. Form a golden fist with the hand of wisdom (*prajñā-hasta*) and place it above the brow.
The mantra of the Tathāgata’s ūrṇā-kośa (hair-treasure) is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānām aṃ jaḥ*. Next, the general seed-heart-mantra of all the Honored Ones is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ ka*. Regarding the letter-gateway *ka* as taught in the sūtras: "All dharmas are without fabrication."
The seal of the Cintāmaṇi-ratna King: the five wheels of concentration and wisdom interlace with one another.
This symbolic form of the vajra-pañjali mudrā pervades all the dharmas of the Bodhisattvas.
The mantra of all Bodhisattvas is as follows:
Acala removes defilement, expelling obstacles and causing [the practice] to shine forth;
to pacify all hindrances, he abides in the fire-born samādhi.
The mantra of Acala’s messenger for purifying all offerings by means of the Wisdom Sword mudrā is as follows:

"Namaḥ samantabhadra-jvara-canda-mahā-ruṣa-nāśa-sphoṭaya hūṃ trāṭ phaṭ hūṃ hūṃ mā hūṃ. For the demarcation of the boundaries of the directions and sub-directions, the Wisdom Sword is used in all cases.
Next, perform the rite of invocation: Form the firm Vajra-bond, extend the two wind-wheels straight, and bend their upper joints downward.
This is called the Vajra Hook, which is able to summon all assemblies.
The Noble Ones come by virtue of their vows, Not transgressing their original samaya.
The mantra for summoning the noble assembly is as follows:
Next, one offers the samaya, Fully employing the mantras and mudrās.
The mudrās and signs are as previously explained; these are the teachings on the various samayas.
The samaya mantra is as follows:
Next, offer arghya water, presenting it to all the Sugatas.
Use this for bathing the stainless body.
The *argha* mantra is as follows:
Next, offer the lotus seat, placing it everywhere.
The two voids and the earth-wheel (pṛthivī-maṇḍala) are joined together to form the pedestal;
the remaining wheels are each situated at a distance from one another—this is the Lotus Seal (*padma-mudrā*).
The mantra for the Tathāgata’s seat is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām āḥ*. Furthermore, one should perform the ritual of expulsion using the Great Wisdom Sword Mudrā.
One should contemplate the mantra of the Noble Acala as being identical to that [previous form].
With the most supreme vajra-flame, one burns all obstacles without remainder;
immediately thereafter, one should transform into the body of Vajrasattva.
In union with mantra and mudrā, pervading all the limbs.
The seed-syllable of Vajra-hṛdaya is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vaṃ*. Contemplating this true meaning, all phenomena are beyond verbal expression.
Because he is endowed with the seals and so forth, he is identical to Vajradhara.
One should know that the form of his seal consists of five prongs within the water-circle.
The mantra of Vajrasattva is as follows:
Next, one should completely cover the body with the adamantine armor;
the secret mudrās of body and speech have already been explained according to the ritual.
Next, the syllable Kha, provided with a bindu, should be placed upon the crown of the head.
Contemplating this mantra, one realizes that all phenomena are like space.
That mantra is as follows:
Next, one should abide with a single mind in the seal for subduing all māras.
The wise one should universally transform [the ground], making it correspond with the mantra.
All those who harbor evil intentions shall see the blazing light of vajra flames pervading this entire earth.
Then, forming the vajra-fist, extend the wind-wheel (the index finger) straight upward and place it at the limit of the white tuft;
having the form of Vajrapāṇi, this is his insignia.
This mudrā is named the Great Seal; by reciting it, one eliminates all demons.
The mantra of Bhṛkuṭī is as follows:
Next, employ the Unbearable One, together with the secret mudrā and mantra.
And by means of this, one binds the perimeter; its majestic ferocity is such that none can behold it.
First, with the three *puṭas*, place the wind-mudrā (*vāyu-cakra*) upon the palm;
the two space-mudrās (*ākāśa-cakra*) and the earth-mudrā (*pṛthivī-cakra*) are bent inward like hooks.
The fire-wheel merges to form a peak, and the water-wheel opens and disperses;
rotating and pointing toward the ten directions—this is called binding the great boundary (*mahā-sīmā-bandha*).
The mantra of the Invincible One (*Aparājita*) is as follows:
Or, by means of Acala, one accomplishes all tasks,
purifies the body and the dwelling place, and binds the boundaries of the various directions.
The seed-syllable heart-mantra of Acala is as follows:
Forming that seal of the sword of wisdom, sprinkle [the offerings] everywhere;
these various incenses, flowers, and so forth are the requisites for worship prepared.
Furthermore, place them all pervasively with the mind of the pure dharma-realm.
As for what is called the gateway of the letter *la*, it is as previously revealed.
The mantra for scented ointment (*vilepana*) is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ viśodhakandhodvapā svāhā.* The mantra for scattering flowers (*puṣpa*) is:
The mantra for incense is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ mahā-maitrī-tārjite svāhā*. The mantra for lighting the lamp is: *Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ dharma-dhātu-nāgite svāhā*.
*Namo samantabuddhānām | tathāgatārhatsamyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ gagaṇodariye svāhā.* The mantra for offering food is as follows: Whatever other articles of worship there may be that ought to be offered,
according to this ritual procedure, they should be purified by the Lord Acala.
Join the palms of concentration and wisdom, with the five wheels interlaced;
this is the seal for holding various objects, the universal seal of offering.
Again, perform the ritual of the heart-mind, and all that is offered will be fully perfected.
In this realm and in all other realms, clouds of great offerings and adornments each rain down various articles of worship, making offerings to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions.
By means of the seal of the Empowerment of the Treasury of Space,
Whatever matters are cultivated according to the Dharma,
Accumulating all merits and dedicating them toward the attainment of *siddhi*, Is for the benefit of all sentient beings.
If any practitioners of mantras Seek *siddhi* in this very life,
First, perform the recitation according to the ritual; once that which was to be done is completed,
further offer worship to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with the sublime chanting of Vajradhara, and you shall swiftly attain accomplishment.
The Vajra Song of Praise says:
"Because of being embraced by Vajrasattva, May I become the unsurpassed Vajra Jewel;
Through the singing of Vajra words, May the supreme Vajra activity be accomplished."
The Verse of the Transformation Consort says:
“Adorned by my own merit, Born from within the pure realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu),
And sustained by the spiritual power of the Tathāgata, I shall accomplish all the aims and benefits of sentient beings.”
Recite the *Ākāśagarbha-vajra-vidyā* three times; the form of the secret mudrā is as previously described.
Having thus completed the ritual offerings, arouse the mind that seeks to benefit inexhaustible sentient beings.
Prostrate to all Buddhas, noble deities, and others, then sit upon the seat of correspondence and enter into *samādhi*.
The ritual procedure of the four dhyānas can bring joy and bliss to the inner mind;
through the empowerment of the ultimate truth, one shall attain samādhi in the mantra.
The wise one, as previously instructed, visualizes before them their own chosen deity;
within the luminous full moon of that mind, they clearly perceive all the syllables of the mantra.

The practitioner should give rise to a resolute mind; first, with single-pointed focus, they should visualize the tutelary deity, maintaining its mantra and secret mudrā, and manifest themselves as the yoga-form of the tutelary deity.
By abiding in the body associated with the fundamental stage, even those of meager merit shall achieve accomplishment.
If a practitioner recites the mantra and mudrā of the Perfectly Awakened Mahāvairocana, they should rely upon this very method.
The seed-syllable heart-mantra of Mahāvairocana is as follows:
Regarding the body-seal (kāyamudrā) therein, it is the mark of the White Urna of Perfect Enlightenment;
the hand of wisdom forms a vajra-fist, positioned between the eyebrows.
The mantra for the ūrṇā-kośa (ūrṇā-lakṣaṇa) of the Tathāgata is as follows:
As before, one transforms the letter A to become the Honored One Mahāvairocana;
because it is sustained by the power of the Dharma, he is no different from one’s own body.
Abiding in the yoga of the deity, one adds the syllables of the five limbs to the lower body,
above the navel, the heart, the crown, and the space between the eyebrows;
while in samāhita, one establishes them through mental visualization.
By abiding in reliance upon this Dharma, one is identical to the Honored Muni.
With the syllable A added to the lower body, there is the yoga-seat of the golden wheel;
with the syllable Vaṃ added above the navel, there is the water of great compassion, pure and white in radiance.
The syllable *laṃ*, with the mind-position added, is the fire-light of red-cornered wisdom;
the syllable *haṃ* at the limit of the white tuft is the sovereign power of the black wind;
the syllable *kha* is upon the crown of the head, the five colors named Great Space.
The five syllables adorn the body; majesty and virtue are perfected. Blazing with the great light of wisdom, they eliminate all karmic offenses.
Upon seeing this person’s brilliance, the armies of Māra and the heavenly demons retreat.
The syllable *Taṃ* signifies the Great Compassionate Void-Pinnacle; because its boundless nature is empty and unobstructed.

Just as the realm of space is free from all conceptualization and is non-conceptual, so too is the sublime contemplation of the wisdom of all-knowledge equal and free from all conceptualization and non-conceptualization; therefore, it is called "unequaled with the unequaled."
The syllable *HŪṂ* represents the cause; it is the "forehead of the wind of great compassion," for the wind of wisdom is able to bring about development.

Just as the wind can thoroughly cleanse away dust, mist, smoke, and clouds, so too does the wind of great wisdom thoroughly cleanse the impurities of ignorance, the afflictions (*kleśa*), mental dullness (*styāna*), and so forth.
The seed-syllable 𑀯 (ra) represents the heart of great compassion-fire; because it is nurtured by the torch of samādhi and wisdom, it is like fire that can burn all fuel.

In the same way, the fire of omniscience burns the fuel of ignorance, extinguishing the defilements of deluded karma without remainder, and serves as a great illumination within the darkness of nescience.
The syllable *Vam* signifies the navel of Great Compassion, for it is nourished by the ocean of milk of merit.
Just as water flows from high to low, bringing great benefit by moistening and nourishing grasses, trees, flowers, and fruits, and being pure by nature;

so too does the water of the Tathāgata’s wisdom flow from the *dharmadhātu* of mantras toward the world, moistening all dharmas that sustain life and assist the path, bringing them to fruition as great fruits, and constantly washing the bodhicitta so that it is not defiled.
The seat is the ground-element of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā-bhūmi*), for it is sustained by the adamantine jewel-ground beneath the vajrāsana.

Just as the earth can give birth to all things and bears the weight of the entire world without being shaken, so too does the ground of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*) arise from the adamantine nature of the Tathāgata; that which thus arises is ultimately non-arising, yet it can produce the myriad virtues of bodhi and sustain the mental ground of all worthies and sages, being indestructible.
Furthermore, place the King of Pervasive Radiance of a Hundred Lights within the head;
place the syllable "Vimala" (the Stainless) in the eyes, like a lamp shining with clear brilliance.
When the wise contemplate their own body, it is identical to the body of the Tathāgata.
In the place where the moon of the mind is perfectly bright, the garland of sounds is in resonance.
Each syllable is without interruption, like the chiming of bells;
this mantra of the Perfectly Awakened One should be taken up and upheld as one pleases.
One should know that through these skillful means, one will swiftly attain *siddhi*.
Alternatively, it is said that by following other ritual procedures, the common gateway of the three mysteries is entered;
if one understands how to revolve [the mantras], all that is performed will be accomplished.
The Heart Mantra of the Universal Seed is as follows:
Through the light of this principle, contemplate the true meaning of these sounds;
with the seal of the King of Maṇi Jewels, concentration and wisdom are interwoven.
The mantra of all Bodhisattvas is as follows:
The syllable *kha* contains all colors; by adding the great dot (*bindu*) of space and placing it upon the crown, one shall attain equality with space.
Furthermore, within its head, one should visualize the primordial syllable, adorned with a pure white bindu, the most excellent heart-mantra of the hundred vidyās.
The visual faculty is like a bright lamp; it is the stainless syllable of the great void.
Abiding in the state of the deity, the Perfectly Awakened One shall manifest before one.
Furthermore, one visualizes at the site of that heart a perfectly pure lunar disc,
upon which the gateway of the letter A appears vividly, pervading all with the color of vajra.
The meaning of its sound is reality: all phenomena are fundamentally unarisen.
With the letter Ka as its head, it is the reality that is upheld;
arranged in a circle, it is perfectly luminous.
Entering and exiting at will, one should then perform the recitation until exhaustion,
after which one should cease.
Within the moon-disk of the mind, one should act according to its profound and secret intent.
Contemplate the reality of sound;
or, by offering incense, flowers, and so forth, perform the worship in successive order.
One should act as previously described, performing the self-consecration.
The body of Vajrasattva possesses immeasurable virtues; toward inexhaustible sentient beings,
he gives rise to a heart of great compassion.
And with other sublime words, they praise the true virtues of all Tathāgatas.
Having dedicated the merit of their virtuous deeds, they make this aspiration:
"Just as the Great Awakened World-Honored One, by means of the merits he has realized, dedicates them toward great bodhi;
so do I now likewise take all my accumulated merit and,
together with the sentient beings of the dharma-realm, cross over the ocean of birth and death."
He attains the state of Perfectly Complete Enlightenment, the Dharma that benefits both self and others,
and dwells in the Great Abode of the Tathāgata— not merely for his own sake,
but until he returns to the cycle of birth and death to deliver all sentient beings.
Having attained all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) and reached the supreme bliss,
one should offer *argha* water.
Visualizing the assembly of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas placed upon the crown of one's head, one should contemplate them.
With true and great merit, he spoke these words of sincere homage.
He uttered this verse of salutation:
“Those who have forever departed from all faults, Whose bodies are adorned with immeasurable virtues, I pay homage.”
"To those who are solely devoted to benefiting sentient beings, I now offer my life and pay homage to them all.
Next, he addressed the assembly of holy ones, speaking these verses:
"To all the Tathāgatas present before us, and to all the Bodhisattvas who save the world,"
May those who do not sever the Mahāyāna teachings and have reached the most excellent state—
may the assembly of noble devas certainly bear witness to me;
each may abide as they please, yet hereafter, may you again deign to come out of compassion.
Next, one should release the samaya-mantra and mudrā from the crown of the head while generating this thought:
"May all bonds, protections, and empowerments be brought to liberation."
By this skillful means, the various honored ones previously invited each returned to their respective abodes, for they were not detained by the unimpeded great vow.

Furthermore, by means of the empowerment of the intrinsic nature of the dharmadhātu upon one's own body, one contemplates the pure bodhicitta and abides in the body of Vajrasattva; herein lies the vidyā-mudrā.

As previously stated, once the recitation is completed, one should sustain the body with these three seals; thus, all gateways of mantra practice are concluded, and the ritual procedures are entirely perfected.

Furthermore, one should employ the aforementioned skillful means to contemplate the syllable *dharmadhātu* as the mark of the crown, donning the adamantine armor; through this secret adornment, one immediately attains an adamantine self-nature that cannot be obstructed or destroyed by anything.

All those who hear his voice—whether they see him, or touch him—will all certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and fully accomplish all merits, becoming equal to the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana without any difference.

Next, one should further arouse the superior mind (*adhimukti-citta*) and perform sublime activities: adorn a pure place with incense and flowers; first cause oneself to become Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva or abide in the self-nature (*tathāgata-svabhāva*) of the Tathāgata; relying on the aforementioned skillful means, empower [the site] with mantras and secret mudrās; thereafter, with a mind intent on the gift of Dharma (*dharma-dāna*), recite or mentally chant Mahāyāna Vaipulya sūtras, and request the various devas and spirits to listen and receive them.
As it is said in the verse:
"The *Vajraśekhara Sūtra* states: 'The Lotus-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Is identical to all Buddhas, Possessing a body of inexhaustible adornment.'"
"Or else, taking any one name of the World-Leaders, those who possess mastery over all phenomena,
one should perform the empowerment of the fundamental nature.
The seed-syllable heart-mantra of Avalokiteśvara is as follows:
The gate of syllables is the meaning of reality; all phenomena are free from defilement and attachment.
One should contemplate them as being produced from sound.
Within this, the characteristic of the secret body is the so-called lotus seal.
As previously explained regarding the offering of the seat, I have already analyzed and taught that.
Next, the mantra of Avalokiteśvara is recited as follows:

*Namo maṃtrasamantabuddhānāṃ sarvathātathāgata-vajrarucita-karmanāma-rara-ra-ra-hūṃ jaḥ svāhā.* First, place the syllable of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) upon the crown of the head. Furthermore, apply this mantra and its corresponding mudrā. Then, according to one's capacity, recite the sūtras and dharmas, or construct a *caitya* or maṇḍala.
When what was to be done has been completed, one should next rise from one's seat and attend to the affairs of others with a demeanor of harmony and respect.
Furthermore, in order to sustain the physical body, one should next go for alms—whether invited by a donor or obtained within the Sangha—and should abstain from fish, meat, and pungent vegetables.

Furthermore, after making offerings to one's tutelary deity and the various Buddhas, one must not consume any leftovers, including various types of stale or impure food, nor any fermented liquors, fruit juices, or other drinks capable of causing intoxication.

Next, offer a morsel of food to present to the Honored One, and again perform the ritual for eating at will. If there is any remainder, set aside a portion for the sake of relieving the hunger and poverty of beggars, and generate this thought:

"I accept this solid food in order to maintain this physical vessel so that I may practice the Path in peace; it is like greasing the axle of a carriage so that it does not break and can reach its destination, and not for the sake of flavor."

Having adjusted his mind and formed the intention to produce a lustrous and adorned body, he then visualizes the syllable *HŪṂ* within the dharma-realm, which completely purifies all food, and consecrates his own person with the Karma-vajra.
In this regard, the seed-syllable is as described in the *Vaṃ* mantra; furthermore, one should recite the *Daśabala-dāna-mantra* eight times before consuming it.
This mantra is stated as follows:
*Namo bhagavate bodhisattvānām | Oṃ ma-lan-da-ni-te-ju-ma-ri-ṇi svāhā.* Abiding thus, one first accomplishes the yoga of the tutelary deity (*iṣṭadevatā*).
When the meal is finished, one should offer the remaining edible food with the heart-mantra of Sarvārthasiddhi.
One should then recite the mantra of the Noble Acala once, augmented by Amoghasiddhi’s wrathful power; the recipient will rejoice and shall constantly follow and protect the practitioner.
The mantra for that is:

*Namaḥ samantabhadra vajrānana āmogha-janmamaharūṣaṇe sphoṭaya hūṃ taramaya taramaya hūṃ phaṭ haṃ maṃ*. After he has finished eating, he should rest for a short while; then he should again pay homage to all Buddhas and repent of all his transgressions.
For the sake of purifying the mind, one should thus cultivate these constant practices, even continuing with the recitation of the scriptures as before.

Remaining constantly established in this, one should likewise do so during the latter part of the day; during the first and last watches of the night, one should contemplate the Mahāyāna without interruption.
At the hour of midnight, one should don the vajra armor as previously described through the Karma-vajra, and pay homage to all Buddhas, great Bodhisattvas, and others.
Next, one should cultivate the mind according to the Dharma for the purpose of making offerings, forming this thought:

"For the sake of seeking the causal conditions of the Great Matter for the benefit of all sentient beings, I ought to protect this body and rest for a short time; it is not for the sake of craving the pleasure of sleep."
"First, one should rectify the deportment of the body, placing the two feet one upon the other and lying on the right side.
If the limbs become weary or slack, there is no fault in turning over as one pleases; however, in order to awaken quickly, one should always fix the mind upon light."
Furthermore, one should not lie prostrate upon a bed; on subsequent days, one should likewise practice in this manner.
Because the mantra-holder practices with unflagging regularity and diligent effort, they receive the title of "Bodhisattva practicing the path through the gateway of mantras."

If, while performing the preliminary practices within the method of recitation during the manifestation of the signs of counting, one does not achieve success despite fully cultivating the sublime activities, one should awaken oneself and redouble one's diligence;
one must not give rise to inferior thoughts and say, "This dharma is not suitable for me."
Thus, by extending their resolve and strength, they benefit themselves and others, never allowing such efforts to pass in vain.

Because the practitioner is diligent and sincere without ceasing, the various sages perceive their minds with profound illumination; consequently, they receive the establishment of majestic spiritual power and attain liberation from all obstacles.
Within this, there are two matters that should not be abandoned:
namely, not forsaking the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and the resolve to benefit inexhaustible sentient beings.
Constantly remaining unshakable in the aspiration for omniscience, through these causes and conditions, one will certainly achieve accomplishment (*siddhi*) according to one's kind.
One should always bathe according to the internal Dharma; one should not cling to external methods of purification.
To harbor doubts or regrets regarding the food of touch and so forth—such things as these should not be done.
If, for the sake of maintaining this body, one bathes at the appropriate times to remove all impurities,
following the ritual instructions regarding rivers and other sites, in conjunction with mantras and mudrās.
Purify all waters with the mind of the *dharmadhātu*; according to their use, remain unmoving as Trailokyavijaya.
With mantras and secret mudrās, protect the directions and the equal [realms], abiding in the contemplation of the essential nature of the deity.
Furthermore, one should maintain the purity of the Buddha-land through three revolutions, Always employing single-minded correct contemplation;
Reciting the mantra of the Holy Immovable One and others, The wise person should silently perform the ritual ablution.
The mind of the pure dharma-realm, the seed-syllable of Acala, and the sword mudrā are all as previously described.
The seed-heart-mantra of Trailokyavijaya is as follows:
herein, the "ha" gate has a phonetic principle as previously explained.
As for the minor distinctions, they are known as the signs of purification.
The Honored One who has subdued the three realms employs the ritual of body-secrecy to accomplish enlightened activities through the mudrās of the five wisdom-vajras.
Next, the mantra of Trailokyavijaya is proclaimed:
Having thus bathed and performed the ritual sprinkling for purification, and having equipped oneself with the samaya and protected the limbs [of the body],
one should contemplate the infinite host of noble deities and offer water three times by cupping it in the hands.
To purify body and mind for the sake of benefiting others, I pay homage to the supreme sons born of the Tathāgata,
who have distanced themselves from the three poisons, conceptual discrimination, and the like, and who have calmed and disciplined their faculties as they enter the chamber of refinement.
Alternatively, relying on the water-chamber as an expedient means, one should abide in the mind according to the ritual previously prescribed;
taking the three equalities as the limit for one’s own body, this is for the sake of seeking the superior, middling, and inferior dharmas.
When the practitioner performs recitation in this manner, all streams of transgression shall forever cease;
they will certainly achieve the dispelling of all obstacles, and the syllables of omniscience will gather within their body.
Relying upon the "Chapter on Worldly Accomplishment" (*Lokasiddhipaṭala*) or what is taught in other sūtras,
one practices the various skillful means of the branches of worship according to their proper sequence.
Because one has not yet departed from the various marks of the conditioned, this is called the *siddhi* of the world;
next, the markless, which is most excellent, is explained—that which is observed by those possessed of faith and understanding.
If a person of profound wisdom in the Mantra Vehicle aspires in this life to seek the unsurpassed fruit,
they should practice contemplation according to their own faith and understanding, following the previously described ritual for mental offerings.
Furthermore, regarding the chapter on the emanation of siddhis and the yoga methods of the supramundane chapter:
he [abides] in the phrase of true dependent origination, with the internal mental factors separated from objective referents.
By practicing and realizing according to these skillful means, one shall attain supramundane accomplishment.
As stated in the Udana verse: "The profound, signless Dharma / Is beyond the capacity of those with inferior wisdom."
"In order to accord with them, / The teaching of having characteristics is also maintained.
